messages.author: b8f5a3439e2d79e5
messages.subject: num_cores_to_use ignored
parts:
Dear all,

When running BioBeoBEARS analyses on our server, the actual input for the num_cores_to_use setting is ignored and the process instead uses all available cores.
When I set BioGeoBEARS_run_object$num_cores_to_use = 12 (or any other number), the analysis will use the total amount of 64 cores.
This server is shared between users and this would limit other users when this analysis takes up all the cores.

Kind regards,
Sander

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] num_cores_to_use ignored
parts:
Hi -- that's very weird and I don't have an explanation.  num_cores_to_use is just passed to standard R functions for parallel processing, BioGeoBEARS is just using standard R functions for that.

Does it happen if BioGeoBEARS_run_object$num_cores_to_use = 1?

Cheers,
Nick

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] num_cores_to_use ignored
parts:
I think this has to be some server-side setting that automatically uses all cores or something -- or you decide the number of cores available from outside of R, before you start R on the server, as I've never seen this before.  The more common issue is e.g. R.app will only do 1 core no matter what the setting is. If you want you can search the code files on num_cores_to_use and find the exact line that opens the processors, and try playing with that command on the server to see if it is malfunctioning.  It is part of R's snow package I think.

Cheers,
Nick
